result.summary: Implements the BIP 54 (Consensus Cleanup) validation rules in Bitcoin Core, defining a BIP 9 versionbits deployment on bit 3 named consensuscleanup. The rules are configured to be always active on regtest and never active on mainnet, testnet, or signet. The implementation enforces a 2,500 non-witness sigops limit per transaction, invalidates 64-byte transactions, requires coinbase transactions to be timelocked to block height minus one with non-final sequence numbers, and constrains block timestamps to prevent timewarp attacks and negative difficulty adjustment intervals.
result.problem: Bitcoin consensus retains known vulnerabilities and algorithmic weaknesses: quadratic legacy sigops CPU exhaustion, Merkle tree leaf-versus-internal node collisions for 64-byte transactions (CVE-2017-12842), and timewarp or negative difficulty adjustments that can manipulate proof-of-work retargeting. Bitcoin Core currently has no implementation or comprehensive regression test harness for BIP 54, making it impossible to evaluate or prepare the consensus cleanup soft fork within the upstream repository.
evidence: The underlying validation rules address documented consensus flaws, including CVE-2017-12842 (Merkle tree ambiguity) and CPU exhaustion from unconstrained legacy script sigops.

PR description notes the code was previously implemented, reviewed, and tested on Bitcoin Inquisition (PRs #99 and #110, plus Delving Bitcoin demonstrations of slow blocks on signet) before being brought upstream with improved tests and test vectors.

enables: Testing of BIP 54 rules on regtest and future evaluation for testnet/signet/mainnet deployment

result.scope_notes: Roughly 95% of the diff is test code, unit test vectors, JSON test data files (bip54_timestamps.json and bip54_coinbases.json), and fuzz testing. Consensus-critical logic changes are confined to src/consensus/ and src/validation.cpp.
result.changed_since_previous: Rebased with minor test adjustments, such as separating 63-byte and 64-byte functional tests and updating functional test framework coinbase creation scripts.
result.card: This PR implements BIP 54 (Consensus Cleanup) validation rules, configured as active exclusively on regtest and never active on mainnet, testnet, or signet. The soft fork rules mitigate legacy sigops CPU exhaustion by capping non-witness sigops at 2,500 per transaction, invalidate 64-byte transactions to prevent Merkle tree collisions, require coinbases to be timelocked to block height minus one, and restrict block timestamps to prevent timewarp and negative difficulty adjustments. Over 95% of the diff consists of test vectors, unit tests, a fuzzing target, and functional tests ported and improved from Bitcoin Inquisition. This enables full in-tree testing and review of the consensus cleanup proposal without altering consensus rules on live networks.

risk.why: Mistakes in consensus validation logic or block connection rules could cause consensus divergence or consensus failure if activated.
